dedupe_keys.name: japan cabinet secretariat guidance on responding to large scale infrastructure failures with especially serious social impact

description: This guidance sets out how Japan's national and local governments should respond, together with major infrastructure operators, to large-scale failures of electricity, communications, transport and other infrastructure caused by something other than a natural disaster, such as a cyber attack, a software malfunction or human error, when the social impact is especially serious. It is a decision of the inter-ministerial liaison meeting run by the Cabinet Secretariat, which first met on 10 February 2025 and met again in June 2025 and April 2026. The 31-page document lists knock-on effects of a long blackout or water outage, such as stopped payments, remote monitoring and logistics, and effects on hospitals and food and drug plants; explains when the Disaster Countermeasures Basic Act and the Disaster Relief Act apply, for example shelters, food and water, medical care and welfare; and covers emergency power at key facilities, priorities and suspected cyber attacks. The meeting page also posts a tabletop exercise, its results and an example damage and response timeline. Coverage is Japan. Format and access: free Japanese PDFs. Licence: not stated. Caveats: it is a policy framework without quantified scenarios. It frames emergency response and cascading failure studies of non-natural infrastructure outages. A related catalogue record is the Cabinet Office Tohoku lifeline restoration data.
